IT 505 · Fundamentals of Database Technologies · lab environment, guide 4 of 4

Guide 4 · AWS Academy: managed services and the cloud twin

The same course, in the cloud. Part A creates the database families as managed AWS (Amazon Web Services) services with one command. Part B builds the twin of your virtual machine on one cloud server with the installer of Guide 3. A third command brings the twin back, with your data, whenever a limit of AWS Academy has ended it.

about 45 minutesAWS Academy Learner Lab8 animations22 actions3 files: it505_aws.sh, it505_setup.sh, template
How to use this guide. Work from top to bottom and tick each action when it is done; the page remembers your ticks on this computer. Each animation starts by itself, can be paused and stepped through one instruction at a time, and can be saved as a GIF (Graphics Interchange Format) picture file with its Download button. The menu stays at the top while you scroll; every section can be folded with its own button or with the floating button at the bottom right. In the dark boxes, a line that begins with # or -- explains the command below it; the Copy button of a terminal box copies the command without that line.
This guide is a Cyber.SoHo educational material. Its use is governed by the Legal Notice, Terms of Use and Acceptable Use Policy of Cyber.SoHo. You install software on your own equipment on your own responsibility; check every download as described in the guide. Details are in the section Legal at the end.
Start

Your AWS Academy courses, the limits, and the plan

Which existing lab covers which family · what the Learner Lab allows · what it costs
Why this step. AWS (Amazon Web Services) Academy gives every student a temporary AWS account. Used well, it shows how the databases of the course are offered as services; used carelessly, its budget is gone in a weekend. This section is the map.

1. The guided labs you already have

Several of your AWS Academy courses already contain a guided lab for a database family. Such a lab comes with its own instructions and its own short-lived account, which is erased when the lab ends. It is suitable as a demonstration or as home practice. It uses AWS's own scenario, not the data of this course.

Database familyAWS serviceGuided lab in your course listWith the data of this course

Key-value and documentAmazon DynamoDBAWS Academy Cloud Developing [64884], Module 5: lab Working with Amazon DynamoDB.Part A: the table it505-orders
Flat files and SQL (Structured Query Language) on filesAmazon S3 (Simple Storage Service) with Amazon AthenaAWS Academy Cloud Developing [64884]: lab Working with Amazon S3. AWS Academy Data Engineering [64707], Module 4: lab Querying Data by Using Athena.Part A: the bucket and the Athena workgroup
Big dataAWS Glue, Amazon EMR (Elastic MapReduce), Amazon RedshiftAWS Academy Data Engineering [64707]: labs Performing ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) on a Dataset by Using AWS Glue, Processing Logs by Using Amazon EMR, Storing and Analyzing Data by Using Amazon Redshift. AWS Academy Lab Project - Cloud Data Pipeline Builder [64994]: an unguided project on website click data.Part B: Spark and DuckDB on the twin

For the professorThe lab titles above come from published course outlines and student write-ups, not from your educator pages, which cannot be opened without your login. Open Modules in each course and confirm the titles before you announce them. To give students access you create a class from the course and invite them; the course Educator Getting Started with AWS Academy of your list describes that procedure. For the work of this guide one class is enough: AWS Academy Learner Lab (course code ALLv2EN-US-83602 in your list).

2. The limits of the Learner Lab

LimitValueWhat happens at the limitAnswer of this guide
Session4 hours; choosing Start Lab again resets the timerRunning EC2 (Elastic Compute Cloud) instances may be stopped. Their disks and everything else are kept. After a new start the instance has a new public address.bash it505_aws.sh start prints the new address.
BudgetA fixed amount per student, shown at the top of the lab page: USD (United States dollar) 50 in recent classes, USD 100 in older descriptions. The display is updated only every 8 to 12 hours.When it is used up, the lab account is disabled and everything in it is lost.Stop what you do not use; keep a backup on your own computer; rebuild restores the twin in a new account.
Regionsus-east-1 (N. Virginia) and us-west-2 (Oregon)Requests elsewhere are refused.The script works in the Region of your console.
EC2Instance sizes nano to large; at most 9 instances and 32 virtual processors; disks up to 100 GB (gigabyte)Larger requests are refused or the instance is terminated.The twin is one t3.medium (2 processors, 4 GB) with a 30 GB disk; --size large gives 8 GB.
Amazon RDSSizes nano to medium; engines Aurora, MySQL, PostgreSQL, MariaDB; up to 100 GB of gp2 storage; one zone; no enhanced monitoringA stopped database is started again automatically after seven days and then costs money.The template obeys every restriction; services-down deletes the database.
IAM (Identity and Access Management)No new users or groups, and no roles of your own; the ready-made LabRole and LabInstanceProfile are to be usedRequests are refused.The scripts create no IAM resource.
End of the classThe end date set by the educatorThe account and its content are deleted.Download a backup before that date.

The Readme inside your own lab is the authority: AWS Academy changes these values from time to time. The table follows the document AWS Academy Learner Lab - Foundation Services published by AWS and the lab pages of courses that used the Learner Lab in 2025 and 2026.

3. What it costs

ResourceApproximate price in us-east-1In practice

AttentionThese are on-demand prices for us-east-1, rounded. They agree with public price lists read on 21 November 2026: USD 0.0416 per hour for a t3.medium, about USD 13 per month for a db.t3.micro with PostgreSQL, USD 0.115 per GB and month for its storage. AWS's own pricing pages, linked at the end, are the authority; they did not show their tables to an automated reader, so look at them yourself before you plan a budget.
Your choice of toolsEvery tool in this guide is open-source software, and every one is a proposal. You may replace any of them with another suitable tool that is available to you, provided that you can justify the choice. Research your tools thoroughly: read the licence, the documentation and the date of the last release. Be creative; you may even build a tool of your own. In the cloud the same holds for services: Part A uses the simplest AWS service for each family; others exist.
Step 1

Start the lab and open CloudShell

Actions 1 to 3 · 5 minutes
Why this step. The lab page creates your temporary AWS (Amazon Web Services) account and signs you in. CloudShell is a terminal inside that account: it needs no installation and no access keys on your own computer.

Sign in to AWS Academy, open the course AWS Academy Learner Lab, choose Modules, then Launch AWS Academy Learner Lab.

Choose Start Lab and wait until the dot beside the word AWS is green (one to two minutes the first time). Then click AWS. The AWS console opens in a new browser tab; allow the pop-up if the browser asks.

At the top right the Region must read N. Virginia (us-east-1). Open CloudShell with the icon >_ in the top bar and wait for the prompt.

✔ Done when: CloudShell shows a prompt that begins with [cloudshell-user@.
Step 2

Upload the kit and check the account

Actions 4 to 6 · 3 minutes
Why this step. The kit is one small file with the three files that do the work. Uploading it to CloudShell puts them where the commands of this guide expect them.

it505_aws.sh, it505_setup.sh, it505_managed_services.yaml, a test file and a README · 47 KB (kilobyte)

Download the kit to your own computer with the button above. In CloudShell choose Actions > Upload file and select IT505_AWS_Kit.zip.

Unpack the kit.

CloudShell
# Unpack the kit; -o replaces older copies of the same files without asking.
unzip -o IT505_AWS_Kit.zip

Ask the script who you are and what exists already. The line Identity should contain the word voclabs.

CloudShell
# Show the account, the Region and what exists already; nothing is created.
bash it505_aws.sh check
Good to knowCloudShell keeps the files of its home folder between sessions, for each Region separately. It loses them when the lab account is reset; then you upload the kit again.
✔ Done when: the check prints your account number and Machine : none.
Step 3

Part A: the database families as managed services

Actions 7 to 12 · 30 minutes, 10 of them waiting
Why this step. A managed service is a database that the cloud provider installs, patches and backs up for you; you receive an address and a password. Seeing the same SQL (Structured Query Language) run against it shows what changes when the server is no longer yours, and what does not.

Create the services. The script asks for the public internet address of your own computer: open checkip.amazonaws.com in a new browser tab and type the number shown. Then wait 6 to 10 minutes.

CloudShell
# Create the managed services of Part A from the description in the file it505_managed_services.yaml.
bash it505_aws.sh services-up

The script hands the file it505_managed_services.yaml to AWS CloudFormation, the service that creates resources from a written description. The description contains a PostgreSQL server on Amazon RDS (Relational Database Service), a table in Amazon DynamoDB, a private bucket in Amazon S3 (Simple Storage Service) and, in a second step, a workgroup of Amazon Athena with a database in the AWS Glue Data Catalog. Every line of the description carries a comment that explains it.

Relational. In your virtual machine open DBeaver, create a PostgreSQL connection as in Guide 3, step 3, and use the host, user and password that the script printed. Or use the terminal of the VM (Virtual Machine):

Terminal of your VM
# Connect to the PostgreSQL server on RDS over an encrypted connection (sslmode=require) and ask for its version.
psql "host=PASTE-THE-RDS-HOST port=5432 dbname=mercadillo user=it505 sslmode=require" -c "SELECT version();"

Key-value and document. In CloudShell write one item into the DynamoDB table, read it back by its key, and ask for every item of one group.

CloudShell
# Write one item. The keys pk and sk identify it; item and quantity are its other attributes.
aws dynamodb put-item --table-name it505-orders --item '{"pk":{"S":"BASKET#77"},"sk":{"S":"ITEM#1"},"item":{"S":"notebook"},"quantity":{"N":"2"}}'
CloudShell
# Read the same item back by its complete key.
aws dynamodb get-item --table-name it505-orders --key '{"pk":{"S":"BASKET#77"},"sk":{"S":"ITEM#1"}}'
CloudShell
# Ask for every item whose key pk is BASKET#77.
aws dynamodb query --table-name it505-orders --key-condition-expression "pk = :b" --expression-attribute-values '{":b":{"S":"BASKET#77"}}'

Flat files. Copy the five-row test file of the kit into the bucket.

CloudShell
# Ask CloudFormation for the name of the bucket and keep it in the variable BUCKET.
BUCKET=$(aws cloudformation describe-stacks --stack-name it505-services --query "Stacks[0].Outputs[?OutputKey=='BucketName'].OutputValue" --output text)
# Copy the test file into the folder smoke/ of the bucket.
aws s3 cp it505_smoke_test.csv s3://$BUCKET/smoke/
# Print the bucket name; you need it in the next action.
echo $BUCKET

SQL on files. Open the service Athena in the console, choose the workgroup it505 at the top right of the query editor and the database it505 at the left. Athena accepts one statement at a time: copy the first, put your bucket name in place of BUCKET, choose Run, then do the same with the second and the third. The lines that begin with -- are explanations: the Copy button leaves them out, and Athena does not need them. Under each result Athena shows how much data it read: compare the CSV (Comma-Separated Values) table with the Parquet table.

SQL for Athena: statement 1
-- Describe the CSV file in the bucket as a table. Nothing is copied: the data stay in the file.
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE IF NOT EXISTS it505.smoke_csv (id int, item string, quantity int, unit_price double)
-- The fields of a line are separated by commas.
ROW FORMAT DELIMITED FIELDS TERMINATED BY ','
-- The folder of the bucket that holds the file.
LOCATION 's3://BUCKET/smoke/'
-- The first line of the file holds the column names, not data.
TBLPROPERTIES ('skip.header.line.count'='1');
SQL for Athena: statement 2
-- Query the file with ordinary SQL: one line total per row, the largest first.
SELECT item, quantity * unit_price AS line_total FROM it505.smoke_csv ORDER BY line_total DESC;
SQL for Athena: statement 3
-- Store the same rows a second time, in the column-oriented Parquet format, as a new table.
CREATE TABLE it505.smoke_parquet WITH (format = 'PARQUET') AS SELECT * FROM it505.smoke_csv;

Delete the services as soon as the exercise is done. The RDS database is charged for every hour that it exists, also after the lab session has ended.

CloudShell
# Delete everything that services-up created, so that nothing is charged any longer.
bash it505_aws.sh services-down
Good to knowIf the lab does not allow Athena or Glue, the script reports it and keeps the other three services; the lab Querying Data by Using Athena of the course AWS Academy Data Engineering then covers that part. The ledger family has no managed service here: use the twin of Part B.
✔ Done when: bash it505_aws.sh services-status answers The managed services do not exist.
Step 4

Part B: the cloud twin of your virtual machine

Actions 13 and 14 · 15 minutes, 12 of them waiting
Why this step. The twin is one cloud server with Debian 13 on which the installer of Guide 3 has run. It serves a student whose laptop cannot run VirtualBox, a class that needs identical machines at once, and a professor who wants to show the tools from any computer.

Create the twin. The script asks for your public address if it does not know it yet, starts the server, copies the installer to it, and shows the installer's progress. Keep the CloudShell tab open and press a key now and then, because CloudShell closes after about 20 minutes without input; the installation continues on the server even then.

CloudShell
# Create the cloud twin: a key pair, firewall rules, one server, then the installer of Guide 3 on it.
bash it505_aws.sh deploy

Read the access card that ends the output: the public address, the address and password of JupyterLab, and the connection data of PostgreSQL. The same card appears at any time with:

CloudShell
# Print the access card of the twin again.
bash it505_aws.sh status
OptionEffect
bash it505_aws.sh deploy --size largeA server with 8 GB (gigabyte) of memory instead of 4 GB, at about twice the hourly price. Useful for the Spark exercise of Class 12.
bash it505_aws.sh deploy --desktopAdds the LXQt desktop and DBeaver on the server. You reach the desktop with a program for RDP (Remote Desktop Protocol) on port 3389: Remote Desktop Connection on Windows, Windows App on macOS, Remmina on Linux. This option was not rehearsed.
bash it505_aws.sh deploy --restore FILELoads a backup file into the new twin at once.

What the script creates, all inside your lab account: a key pair for SSH (Secure Shell), whose private half stays in your CloudShell; a security group that admits the ports 22, 8888 and 5432 from your own address only; one EC2 (Elastic Compute Cloud) instance with the newest official Debian 13 image and a 30 GB disk. If the lab refuses the Debian image, the script uses Ubuntu 24.04, on which the installer also runs.

✔ Done when: the access card shows State : running and three addresses.
Step 5

Connect to the twin

Actions 15 to 17 · 5 minutes
Why this step. The twin has no screen. You reach its tools in three ways: JupyterLab in the browser, DBeaver on your own computer, and a terminal through CloudShell.

JupyterLab. In the browser of your own computer open the address https://ADDRESS:8888 from the access card. The browser warns about the certificate. In Chrome and Edge choose Advanced, then Proceed; in Firefox choose Advanced, then Accept the Risk and Continue. Type the JupyterLab password. JupyterLab gives you notebooks, the files of ~/it505 with upload and download, and, under File > New > Terminal, a terminal in which psql, duckdb, valkey-cli and it505 selftest work as in Guide 3.

DBeaver. In DBeaver on your own computer or in your VM (Virtual Machine) create a PostgreSQL connection with the host, port, database, user and password of the access card. The connection is encrypted with TLS (Transport Layer Security).

Terminal. From CloudShell:

CloudShell
# Open a terminal on the twin through an encrypted connection; leave it with the command exit.
bash it505_aws.sh ssh
AttentionAccept the certificate warning only for the address that your own bash it505_aws.sh status printed a moment ago. The certificate was created by your twin and is confirmed by nobody else; that is why the browser cannot check it. On any other site the same warning means: stop.
Good to knowIf the page does not load at all, your public address has probably changed, for example between campus and home. Tell the twin: bash it505_aws.sh myip.
✔ Done when: JupyterLab shows the folders data, starter and backups of the twin.
Step 6

Back up, download, stop

Actions 18 to 20 · 3 minutes at the end of every session
Why this step. Everything in a lab account can disappear with the account. The only copy that survives is the one on your own computer.

Write a backup of the twin and copy it into CloudShell.

CloudShell
# Write a backup on the twin and copy the file into the folder it505-backups of CloudShell.
bash it505_aws.sh backup

Copy the path printed in the last line. In CloudShell choose Actions > Download file, paste the path, and choose Download. The file is now in the Downloads folder of your own computer.

Stop the twin. Its disk and your data stay; only the disk is charged while it is stopped.

CloudShell
# Stop the twin; its disk and everything on it are kept.
bash it505_aws.sh stop
TipThe same backup file fits both machines. A backup made in your VM (Virtual Machine) with it505 backup can be restored into the twin with bash it505_aws.sh restore FILE, and the other way round with it505 restore FILE.
✔ Done when: the backup file is on your own computer and the twin is stopped.
Step 7

When a limit is reached: back in minutes

Actions 21 and 22 · the restoration scripts
Why this step. Two limits will reach every student sooner or later: the four-hour session and the budget. Neither should cost more than a quarter of an hour.
What happenedWhat you seeWhat to do
The session endedThe timer shows 0:00 and the dot is red. The twin is stopped; nothing is lost.Start Lab, open the console and CloudShell, then bash it505_aws.sh start. Use the new address it prints.
Your internet address changedThe browser and DBeaver no longer reach the twin.bash it505_aws.sh myip
CloudShell lost its files (the key file is missing)The script says that the key file is missing.Upload the kit again, then bash it505_aws.sh rebuild; a running twin is backed up first if it can still be reached.
The budget is used up, or the educator has reset your labA new, empty account. The twin, the services and the files in CloudShell are gone.Upload the kit and your last backup file to CloudShell, then bash it505_aws.sh rebuild FILE.
You want a clean machineNothing is wrong; you want to start again.bash it505_aws.sh rebuild takes a backup, deletes the twin, builds a new one and restores the backup.

After a reset: upload IT505_AWS_Kit.zip and your backup file with Actions > Upload file, then run the two commands with the name of your own file.

CloudShell
# Unpack the kit again.
unzip -o IT505_AWS_Kit.zip
CloudShell
# Build a new twin and load your backup into it; use the name of your own file.
bash it505_aws.sh rebuild it505-backup-20261124-1612.tar.gz

Twelve minutes later, check the result on the twin: open JupyterLab, start a terminal there, and run the self-test.

Terminal of the twin
# On the rebuilt twin: use every tool once and report PASS or FAIL for each.
it505 selftest
For the professorA student whose budget is exhausted needs a new lab environment from you; how to grant one is described in your educator material. Remind the class in every session of the three closing commands: backup, download, stop. When the class ends, ask everybody to run bash it505_aws.sh destroy and bash it505_aws.sh services-down.
✔ Done when: the self-test on the rebuilt twin passes and your tables are back.
Reference

Every command of it505_aws.sh

One line each
CommandWhat it does
bash it505_aws.sh checkShows the account, the Region, and what exists already.
bash it505_aws.sh services-upPart A: creates PostgreSQL on RDS (Relational Database Service), a DynamoDB table, an S3 (Simple Storage Service) bucket, and Athena with Glue where allowed.
bash it505_aws.sh services-statusPrints the addresses and the password of Part A.
bash it505_aws.sh services-downDeletes everything of Part A.
bash it505_aws.sh deployPart B: creates the twin. Options --size small|medium|large, --desktop, --restore FILE.
bash it505_aws.sh statusPrints the access card of the twin.
bash it505_aws.sh start / stopStarts the twin after a new session; stops it before you leave.
bash it505_aws.sh myip [ADDRESS]Admits a new public address of your computer and removes the old one.
bash it505_aws.sh sshOpens a terminal on the twin.
bash it505_aws.sh backupSaves the databases and the course folder of the twin into a file in CloudShell.
bash it505_aws.sh restore FILELoads a backup file into the twin.
bash it505_aws.sh rebuild [FILE]Deletes the twin if one exists, builds a new one, and restores a backup.
bash it505_aws.sh installRuns the installer on the twin again, to repeat a failed step.
bash it505_aws.sh destroyDeletes the twin, its security group and its key pair. Backup files in CloudShell are kept.
For the professorHow these scripts were checked. it505_aws.sh was run command by command against a simulated AWS (Amazon Web Services), built with the open-source library moto, with stand-ins for the SSH (Secure Shell) connections: check, deploy, status, myip, backup, restore, stop, start, rebuild in both situations, destroy, services-up, services-status and services-down all completed. The template passes the checker cfn-lint without findings. Both pass ShellCheck. Neither could be run inside a real Learner Lab from the place where it was written. Rehearse Part A and Part B once in your own Learner Lab before the class uses them, and note what your lab's Readme allows.
Help

If something goes wrong

Eight frequent situations, with their cause and remedy
What you seeCause and remedy
AWS does not answerThe lab session has ended. Start Lab, wait for the green dot, open the console from the lab page, open CloudShell again.
Region ...: the Learner Lab allows only us-east-1 and us-west-2The console is set to another Region. Choose N. Virginia at the top right and open CloudShell again.
The instance could not be started, followed by a reasonRead the reason. InstanceLimitExceeded or VcpuLimitExceeded: other instances are running in the account. UnauthorizedOperation: the lab does not allow this request; try --size medium.
The machine does not answer to SSHThe server is still starting. Wait a minute, then bash it505_aws.sh status and bash it505_aws.sh install.
The stack of Part A failsOpen CloudFormation in the console, choose the stack it505-services, tab Events, and read the first line marked CREATE_FAILED. Then run services-up again; the script removes the failed attempt first.
DBeaver cannot reach the RDS (Relational Database Service) host or the twinYour public address is not the one that was admitted. bash it505_aws.sh myip; for Part A run services-up again with the new address.
The browser shows This site can't be reached for port 8888The twin is stopped, or the address is the old one. bash it505_aws.sh start prints the current address.
The budget shrinks faster than expectedSomething is running that you forgot, usually the RDS database of Part A. bash it505_aws.sh check, then services-down and stop.

Version notes

  • Every animation is a drawing made for this guide from the official documentation of each product; none is a screenshot of the product. Labels, colours and positions on your screen will differ in details.
  • Version numbers are those current on 21 November 2026. If you see a newer version, use it: the steps stay the same unless a note in the guide says otherwise.
  • The screens of the AWS Academy lab page and of the AWS console are drawn from their general layout; AWS changes both often.
  • Account numbers, addresses, identifiers and passwords in the animations are invented examples.
  • A VirtualBox machine cannot be copied into the Learner Lab as it is: the import service of AWS needs a role named vmimport, and the lab does not let you create roles of your own. The twin is therefore rebuilt by the same installer, and your data travel in the backup file.
